QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_8

question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund is close-ended, 6-year tenure + 2-year extension used. Its Liquidation Period of 1 year is also ending. Unliquidated investments remain at 18% of NAV. The Manager proposes entering a Dissolution Period. What investor consent is needed for the Dissolution Period itself?

explanation.text: The Logic: Entering the Dissolution Period requires approval of at least 75% of investors by value of their investment in the existing AIF scheme. This is the same threshold as for in-specie distribution during the Liquidation Period. The Trap: Two-thirds by value (Option B) is the tenure-extension threshold, not the Dissolution Period threshold. Simple majority (Option A) is a generic threshold and does not apply. Unanimous consent (Option D) is not the prescribed rule. Note: The merchant-banker filing (Information Memorandum + Due-Diligence Certificate) for entry into the Dissolution Period must be made before the Liquidation Period expires. Failure to obtain the 75% consent during the Liquidation Period triggers mandatory in-specie distribution at Re. 1 (workbook pp. 357-359).
